brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Something to keep sewing supplies tidy (organized storage with compartments)
requirements.evidence: Built 3-cell cluster (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) with 3 bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments), bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) = 7 compartments total for sorting small notions. Dressed with representative small items via fill_compartments (solder-reel, heap-nuts-div3 etc.) showing compartment use. No sewing-specific props (thread, scissors, needles) exist in catalog, so sewing identity is conveyed only by compartmentalized form, not by staged sewing items.

finish.summary: Compact 3-hex organizer with seven divided compartments for sorting sewing notions — threads, buttons, needles, scissors. Structure verified with capOpenFaces and lockJoints; small workshop props placed to demonstrate compartment use. Sewing-specific props unavailable so function is shown by layout.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
